title: Review: How science works: applications, validation and society; Constant-acceleration equations; Motion graphs; Scalars and vectors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: K03-1#N.16, MS05-1#N.4, NEW-nature-of-science-1#N.9, K03-1#N.12, MS05-1#N.13, NEW-nature-of-science-1#N.8, K03-1#N.5a, NEW-nature-of-science-1#N.3, NEW-nature-of-science-1#N.6. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Gradient of a velocity–time graph; uniform when the line is straight.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: Whole area on a velocity–time graph with every part counted as positive.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Runs from the first tail to the last tip when arrows are drawn tip to tail.

items.label: Displacement
items.clue: Area between a velocity–time line and the time axis, negative below the axis.

questions.stem: A toy car is released from rest on a straight slope and speeds up with constant acceleration. It travels 0.60 m in the first 2.0 s. How far does it travel between t = 4.0 s and t = 6.0 s?

A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: A company's paper on a battery that fully charges in one minute passes peer review. Independent laboratories ask for samples to test, but the company refuses. What is the best judgement about the claim?

options.text: Accept it: peer review has already confirmed that the battery works.
Treat it as unconfirmed: it is not established until others can test it.
Reject it as false: refusing to share samples proves that the battery fails.
Accept it: the company's own repeated tests all gave the same result.

questions.explanation: Correct. Validation needs independent replication by people with no stake in the result.

questions.stem: A student drops a ball from rest from several heights h and times each fall, t. She plots t² (y-axis) against h (x-axis): a straight line through the origin with gradient 0.204 s² m⁻¹. What value of g do the results give?
questions.explanation: h = ½gt² gives t² = (2/g)h, so the gradient is 2/g. g = 2 ÷ 0.204 = 9.80 m s⁻².

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?
A town is deciding whether to allow a new mobile-phone mast near a school. Which question can science answer directly?

options.text: Whether the town's residents should accept the mast
Whether the mast is worth the change to the view from the school
Whether better phone coverage for the town matters more than the residents' worries
Whether radio-wave exposure at the school would be below the recommended limits

questions.explanation: Correct. Exposure can be measured or calculated and compared with limits set from the evidence on harm.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?
Many home smoke alarms contain a tiny sealed source of americium-241, an alpha emitter. Which statement is the best scientific evaluation?

options.text: They should be banned, since no radioactive source in a home is ever acceptable.
The added risk is very small and unlikely; the lives saved by early warning far outweigh it.
They carry no risk at all, because alpha particles cannot pass through skin.
The decision depends only on whether radioactive alarms are cheaper than other types.

questions.explanation: Correct. Alpha particles are stopped by the casing, so harm is unlikely while the source stays sealed. The benefit, warning of fire, is large.

questions.stem: A surprising result passes peer review and is published. Two other laboratories then repeat the experiment: one gets the same result, the other does not. What should scientists conclude?

options.text: The result is established: it passed peer review and one laboratory confirmed it.
The result is disproved: one failed replication outweighs the other evidence.
It is not yet established: the cause of the disagreement must be found and tested.
Two results out of three agree, so the majority view should be accepted.

questions.explanation: Correct. Conflicting replications are checked for faults on both sides, as OPERA's timing was, until the evidence agrees.
